content:
Purpose:
This doc captures the initial UX rationale, wireframe iterations, and backlog grooming for an "Investigation-first" view we’re calling the Invocation Attribution Canvas. Goal: give engineers and SREs a fast, explorable UI to map expensive or high-latency invocations down to individual tokens, model variants, and infrastructure signals so they can root-cause and remediate.

Context and user problems:
- Platform engineers and ML engineers need to answer: why did X invocation cost 10x more than baseline, or why did a single customer see a 2s tail latency?
- Current console shows aggregates (per-route average, per-model) but no interactive token lineage to connect generation behavior to batching, cache hits, model switches, or hardware anomalies.
- Investigations are ad-hoc: download JSON, run script, eyeball token timestamps. We want a fast visual surface to explore and export findings.

Primary personas:
- Platform SRE: triage latency regressions for SLAs
- ML infra engineer: validate model quantization and batch effects
- Customer success / solutions engineer: explain unit-cost anomalies to customers
- Product engineer: check that rollout changes didn’t regress token-level economics

Success metrics (product level):
- Mean time to actionable insight after alert reduced from ≥2 hours -> <30 minutes for top 50% of cases
- >60% of investigations start from query in Console (not offline scripts) within 3 months of launch

Wireframe iterations (notes):
V0 — single-pane waterfall (quick spike)
- Waterfall stacked by token with per-token latency bars and cost stamps.
- Pros: quick build, familiar.
- Cons: doesn’t surface lineage or batch-level metadata clearly; noisy for long responses.

V1 — Canvas with Ripple View + Token Ancestry
- Introduce a canvas where each token is a node positioned in time; tokens draw faint 'flows' to tokens that used their KV cache (ancestry edges).
- Ripple visualization: hovering a token pulses related tokens (same batch, same cache region, or same model variant switch).
- Side-panel shows selected token details: token text, cost (units), model-variant, GPU/CPU time, start/end timestamps, batch_id, cache_hit flag, seq_pos.
- Interaction ideas: pin token to top, add an annotation, open the invocation in session-replay (links to replay).
- Data constraints: only fetch full token ancestry on demand to avoid transferring entire 4k+ token sequences by default.

V2 — Compact Table + Sparkline + Heatband
- Hybrid: top of page is timeline canvas (coarse), bottom is resizable compact table with each token row: index, token text (truncated), cost, latency, cache flag, model-variant, sparkline of per-token latency across the invocation.
- Heatband: color ramp applied to table rows and canvas nodes to quickly highlight high-cost or high-latency tokens. Configurable thresholds for cost-per-token and tail-latency percentiles.
- Compare mode: select two invocations and show token-by-token diff (delta cost, delta latency) aligned by tokenizer offsets. Useful for A/B rollout comparisons.

Interaction patterns & keyboard UX:
- Arrow keys: move token focus left/right; Enter: open details pane; P: pin token; A: add annotation; C: compare (start/stop).
- Copy token sequence to clipboard (escaped) for downstream repro.
- Export CSV/NDJSON with selected token fields.

Instrumentation and data model notes:
- Required fields per token: invocation_id, route, customer_id (hashed), token_index, token_text, token_start_ms, token_end_ms, gpu_ms, cpu_ms, bytes_in/out, model_variant, quantized_flag, batch_id, seq_id, prefix_cache_hit, kv_lookup_ms.
- Sample rate: default 1% full-token capture for host-wide; UI queries can request full capture if available.
- Pre-aggregation endpoints: per-invocation summary (cost, median token latency, 95p latency, tokens_above_threshold) and optional token-chunk endpoints (windowed ranges) to support pagination.

Performance constraints and server-side rules:
- UI should render summary and first 200 tokens in <400ms for typical calls (<=200 tokens).
- For long invocations (>1000 tokens) show progressive loading + chunked canvas.
- Heavy operations (diff, ancestry graph) run as async jobs with progress indicators; provide download when complete.

Visual affordances and microcopy suggestions:
- Heatband legend: "Low / Med / High unit cost" with hover text showing sample per-token USD cost estimation.
- Token tooltip: "Token #{i} — model: {variant} — cache: {hit/miss} — cost: {u}u — latency: {ms}ms".
- Empty state: "No token-level telemetry available for this invocation. Toggle full-capture or check sampled traces."

Accessibility: color contrast for heatband (provide alt pattern), ARIA labels for token nodes, focus ring for keyboard navigation.

Open questions and trade-offs (to discuss in grooming):
- Sampling vs cost: how many invocations can we store full token traces for? Retention policy? (30 days by default, with enterprise add-on).
- Privacy: customer_id should be hashed/pseudonymized by default; provide opt-in cleartext for enterprise with consent.
- Side-effect of pre-aggregation: pre-aggregates may hide microbursts; what thresholds to surface raw capture?
- Backend complexity: ancestry edges require instrumentation from runtime to emit which tokens consumed which KV cache entries — is this available for all backends?

User test plan (initial):
- Recruit 6 platform/infra folks and 3 solutions engineers. Tasks: find highest-cost token in an invocation; align two invocations with model-variant differences and identify cost deltas; pin a token and export notes.
- Success criteria: 80% complete tasks without external tooling; median task time <12 minutes.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Canvas: display per-token timeline + heatband for selected invocation. (RDW-1324 backend + RDW-1502 UI)

- Details pane: shows token-level fields: token_index, token_text (truncated), cost_units, latency_ms, model_variant, prefix_cache_hit.

- Export: CSV/NDJSON exports with all visible token fields and invocation metadata.

- Perf: loading summary + first 200 tokens under 400ms for invocations with <=200 tokens (95th percentile).

Open grooming notes (discussion items):
- Decide default sampling policy and how customers request full captures.
- Add toggle to overlay infra metrics (GPU power, utilization) on the canvas.
- UX: Add quick-filters: "show only cache-miss tokens", "show tokens > X ms", "show tokens with cost > Y units".

Attachments & references:
- Figma file (iterative): https://www.figma.com/file/abcd1234/invocation-attribution-canvas
- Backend proto: git repo PR 847 (telemetry changes)
- Related Jira: RDW-1324, RDW-1378, RDW-1410

Next steps (2-week sprint):
- Spike: implement token ancestry API prototype (Avery + Diego) — 3 days.
- Design: mock up compact table + heatband and keyboard nav (Sofia) — 4 days.
- Backend: instrument prefix cache flag + batch_id in invocation stream (Morgan) — 6 days.
- Put on staging and run user tests with infra folks (Elena) — next iteration.
content_summary: Exploratory UX doc for a new "Invocation Attribution Canvas" to enable token-level cost and latency investigation: wireframe versions, interactions, data model, backlog tasks, and acceptance criteria. Focus on fast triage, pin/annotate, compare mode, and trade-offs around sampling and performance.
